exact_statement: For every finite probability law S on F_2^n, influence sum_i P(S_i=1) is minimal under all invertible affine spectral maps iff p_i<=1/2 and min(P(v.S=1),P(v.S=0))>=max_{i:v_i=1}p_i for every nonzero v. Every n-bit Boolean sign f has a Boolean g on d=affdim(supp(fhat)) bits with H(g)=H(f), I(g)<=I(f), full affine spectral dimension and affine-minimal influence. Thus FEI(K), K>=0, is equivalent at the same K on this reduced class, and its finite dimension caps equal the maximum on the nonempty union of reduced classes with dimensions d<=n (individual classes can be empty). Nondecreasing-deficit affine/compression reductions preserve epsilon-nearness to the finite dimensional deficit cap. A minimal-dimension positive K witness with maximal D_K, K>0, itself has full affine spectral dimension and satisfies all the inequalities, in particular P(S_i=S_j=1)<=min(Inf_i,Inf_j)/2. Epsilon-near n-bit maxima obey p_i<=1/2+epsilon/(2K), m(v)>=p_i-epsilon/K when v_i=1, and pair overlap<=min(p_i,p_j)/2+epsilon/(2K). No physical child bank is replaced by the transformed one.
